LLM_description:
Situation:
A major seismic event and subsequent weather system have disrupted ground lines of communication across the region. Supply Depot Alpha, Supply Depot Bravo, Supply Depot Charlie, Supply Depot Delta, and Supply Depot Echo are operational with varying stock positions and resupply timelines. Priority receiving units include Field Hospital Aurora, Relief Battalion Kestrel, Urban Distribution Team Orion, Coastal Shelter Group Phoenix, and Mountain Outpost Sierra. Key routes are degraded: the north valley corridor is prone to landslides and requires clearance; the coastal highway faces intermittent closures due to debris and high water; the mountain pass requires escorted movement; and urban arterials are congested with civilian traffic and ad hoc closures. Aviation support is limited, so ground convoys remain primary.

Mission:
Distribute critical relief commodities to designated receiving units across the initial response window, meeting essential requirements while minimizing total operational cost (transport, shortage penalties, vehicle deployment, and fixed route security risk costs), and maintaining convoy security and route viability.

Execution/Concept:
- Supply and demand: Each depot will dispatch only within its available daily stocks by supply class. Each receiving unit has essential daily requirements; controlled shortfalls are permissible where necessary but incur penalty costs. Prioritize life-sustaining items and time-critical medical materiel.
- Transport and capacity: Deliveries are planned as direct convoys from depots to units. Loads may be mixed by supply class within vehicles, subject to volumetric constraints. Each deployed vehicle carries a cost and has a fixed capacity; fleet availability per operational period is limited and cannot be exceeded across all assignments.
- Route activation and risk: Activating any route for a given period (sending any vehicles) imposes a fixed security and clearance risk cost regardless of the number of vehicles assigned to that route in that period. Vehicles may only travel on routes that have been activated for that period. Concentrate throughput on fewer activated routes when feasible to amortize risk overheads, provided security and access conditions permit.
- Cost discipline: Transport costs are route- and movement-dependent. Shortage penalties reflect operational risk of unmet need. Vehicle deployment costs and fixed route security risk costs must be weighed against the benefits of additional throughput. Open high-risk corridors only when operational urgency or penalty avoidance justifies the added overhead.
- Constraints and controls: Do not exceed depot daily capacities by supply class. Ensure the total volumetric load moved on any depot-to-unit movement does not exceed the product of vehicle capacity and vehicles assigned. The total fleet assigned across all movements within a period must remain within available vehicles. Route activation decisions will be synchronized with security forces and engineering teams.
- Coordination: The Logistics Coordination Cell will finalize daily allocations, issue convoy taskings, and adjust in response to route assessments, weather updates, and unit consumption reports. Contingency plans will redirect flows if a corridor becomes non-viable during execution.
